sources.note: Compares two training-free intent classifiers built from summary statistics of prefill-time activations against trained heads on the same features, and finds the trade-off is not accuracy but where each fails — trained heads win fine-grained distinctions, statistical ones give better uncertainty on mixed prompts and survive adversarial rephrasing that collapses the trained heads to zero.
sources.title: Training-Free versus Training-Based Intent Classification in LLMs: Accuracy, Robustness, and Failure Modes

sources.note: Trains a difference-of-means direction on short- versus long-horizon answer continuations and steers along it, shifting binary temporal choices, moving the monetary indifference threshold on an untrained task by a factor of 56 at a ten-year delay, and changing a planning benchmark — with matched-norm random controls and an unusually candid account of what the direction may actually encode.
sources.title: Intertemporal Preference Steering in Qwen3 via Contrastive Activation Addition

sources.note: Detects flawed reasoning from residual-stream trajectories by combining layerwise motion with a quantized region reader and a normalized direction reader, rather than probing full states.
sources.title: Reasoning Errors Have a Region and a Direction in the Residual-Stream Trajectory of LLMs

sources.note: Traces the brittleness of multimodal RLVR gains under paraphrase and template change to two properties of the standard objective -- a binary verifier that cannot distinguish a wrong answer from a misformatted one, and a training distribution covering a thin slice of the prompts a deployed model meets -- and fixes both with a trinary reward and an invariance penalty across semantically equivalent prompts.
sources.title: Improving Generalization Robustness of Multimodal RLVR

sources.note: Builds safety-alignment training data by first having an agent jailbreak a strong teacher and only then asking that teacher to explain why the successful attack worked, so the student is supervised on the mechanism of the attack rather than on the refusal.
sources.title: Dual-Adversarial Safety Alignment: Cultivating Intrinsic Threat Comprehension in LRMs

sources.note: Fine-tunes a 1.7B model to read structured summaries of a time series and allocate ensemble weights across candidate forecasters, trained by SFT on rule-generated chains of thought and then by GRPO with a bounded reciprocal reward that keeps a continuous error gap from collapsing the group advantage.
sources.title: REATS: LLM Reasoning-based Ensemble Learning for Adaptive Time Series Forecasting

sources.note: Trains self-correction as a step-level preference problem -- preferring a detect-and-repair continuation over the continuation that would follow if the error went unaddressed -- after first initialising with ordinary step-level preference optimisation, and finds that correcting more often and detecting more errors both anti-correlate with accuracy.
sources.title: Reinforcing Step-level Reasoning for Effective Self-Correction in LLMs

sources.note: A benchmark where each task needs one commonsense step and one math step, on which model accuracy drops nearly 30% relative to solving the steps in isolation while humans show no such gap.
sources.title: AgentCoMa: A Compositional Benchmark Mixing Commonsense and Mathematical Reasoning in Real-World Scenarios

sources.note: Shows that transformers can learn implicit multi-step reasoning over stored knowledge, but only through grokking — extended training far past overfitting — and that whether the resulting circuit generalizes out of distribution depends on the reasoning type, succeeding for comparison and failing for composition.
sources.title: Grokked Transformers are Implicit Reasoners: A Mechanistic Journey to the Edge of Generalization

sources.note: Routes each query to a {model, reasoning budget} configuration by fitting an item response theory model over an evaluation matrix, yielding interpretable query difficulties and configuration abilities, and sending harder queries to higher-ability configurations.
sources.title: RADAR: Reasoning-Ability and Difficulty-Aware Routing for Reasoning LLMs

sources.note: Proves that no computable length-generalization bound exists for transformers of depth two or beyond, and gives a matching exponential bound for the positive fragment that corresponds to fixed-precision transformers.
sources.title: Length Generalization Bounds for Transformers

result.definition: Whether a trained improvement survives a change in the input distribution, and across 11 sources the axis on which the archive's supervision results most often separate. Two patterns recur. Rationale supervision is worth little in domain and a great deal out of it -- 20 to 28 points across four models on a contamination-audited external benchmark, against nothing measurable in domain for strong backbones -- and a controlled human study attributes the measurable effect to language adherence and inspectability rather than to better reasoning. And reasoning helps most where the recovery is needed: one self-correction method's out-of-domain gains reach 10.9 and 8.8 points where its in-domain gains average about one, and removing the reasoning step costs 8.7 percent in distribution and 55.6 percent out. The corpus's caution is that out-of-distribution is a direction, not a place: transfer to three related languages is near-identical in average between two methods while distributed differently across the three; a defect direction fitted on controlled pairs scores 83.3 percent held out on those pairs and 19.6 to 30.0 on real benchmarks; and a correctness predictor falls from 0.87 to 0.60 across three shifts while the structural geometry it was computed from transfers intact.
